form.helpText:
The "User" form is a special form that is used by the administrator to add, modify or remove users of the Action Request (AR) System.
The "User" form is used in conjunction with the "Group" form to provide users with permissions that ultimately determine which operations individual users can perform and which forms and fields they can access.
For more information on the "User" form and the AR System access control, please refer to the Action Request System Workflow Administrator's Guide.

definition.helpText: A unique identification value for each request entering the system. It is created and maintained by the system; however it is possible to attach a string to the value for descriptive purposes. Groups that have neither Change nor View access to the Request ID field will not have access to any other form information, regardless of the permission settings of the other fields.
The name of the user who submitted the request. It is usually the name of the AR System user who was logged in when a request was created. In this case it is the Administrator or a Subadministrator.
The date and time at which the request was created in the system. This field is set by the AR System and cannot be modified.

Use this field to allowing users to change user record information. See the "Allowing Users to Change User Record Information" help topic in the AR SystemAdministrator online help for details on how to use this field.
The name of the user who last altered the request. This field is set by the AR System to the login name of the user who last changed the request. It cannot be modified.
The date the field was last modified. This field is set by the AR System to the time the last change to this request was made. It cannot be modified.
Reserved for AR System future use.

The full name and/or other descriptive text that you want to further describe this user record.
This field is a required field. You must enter data in this field before saving the record.

The name a user allowed to access the AR System will enter in the User Name field on the Login dialog box when logging in to the system.
This field is a required field. You must enter data in this field before saving the record.
The password the user will enter when logging in to the system.
The email address of the user.

The list of access control groups to which the user belongs. Group names are separated by spaces.
Although you make requests to the Group list using the alias (name for a group), the group Ids are stored as integer values separated by semicolons.

The notification method used if the user specifies the default mechanism.
If you choose Alert, make sure that you instruct your users to install Remedy Alert and configure their accounts correctly.
If you choose Email, fill in the Email Address field on this form for the user.

The type of license the user has.
With a read license, your user can read and submit requests within the limitations specified by you. Usually your user will not be able to update existing requests; however, your user may be allowed to update requests he or she created.
With a fixed license, your user can read, submit, and update existing requests within the limitations specified by you. Fixed licenses are permanently associated with a single user name. With this type of license, your user can always access the system.
With a floating license, your user has the same privileges as with the fixed license. However, floating licenses are not attached to any single user name. Only a certain number of licenses are available for use. If no license is available when your user tries to log in, he or she receives a message informing them that no license token is currently available and your user is given access to the system with read-only permission. When a license becomes available, your user receives a message indicating that he or she has been allocated a license.
This field is a required field. You must choose one of the choices (or use the default) before saving the record.

An FTS license enables you to use the Full Text Search capability supported by the AR System. If you are assigned a floating license, you will take one of the license tokens available in the license pool. If no license is available, you will receive a message and be allowed to access the system without using the FTS capability (the system will use the default database search capability). When a license token becomes available, you receive a message indicating that you have been allocated a license token, and you can perform Full Text Searches.
This field is a required field. You must choose one of the choices (or use the default) before saving the record.
When set, this field causes client tools to redirect the user to reset their password.
Timestamp when the password was last changed, set by the system or workflow. This value is significant only if the Password Management Policy is enforced.
This overrides the global setting for the number of days before a password expires that this user will receive a warning.
This overrides the global setting for the maximum number of days a password can remain unchanged before it expires.
Temporary field to hold the days until the password will expire so that the value can be displayed in a message.
The date this user's account will be disabled. This date is calculated according to the password policy and set by system workflow.
This field disables password management for this user account, even if global password management is enabled.

value.characterValue: Disable Password Management For This User

definition.helpText: This overrides the global setting for the number of days after a password expires until it is disabled.
This field provides access to the Password and the Force Password Change fields. It normally includes only the user's name.
This field tells us if global password management is enabled. It is set from the user password management configuration form.

This is the number of days before a password expires that this user will receive a warning. It is set from the User Password Management Configuration form unless it is locally overridden by the Number of Warning Days field in the local record.

This is the maximum number of days a password can remain unchanged for this user before it expires. It is set from the User Password Management Configuration form unless it is locally overridden by the Number o Days Before Expiration field in the local record.

definition.fieldName: Applied Days After Expiration Until Disablement
definition.helpText: This is the number of days after a password expires until it is disabled for this user. It is set from the User Password Management Configuration form unless it is locally overridden by the Days After Expiration Until Disablement field in the local record.

value.characterValue: Applied Days After Expiration Until Disablement

escalation.helpText:
Disable a user account by setting the password to an unknown value.
This escalation has a very strong qualifier; we err on the side of not disabling an account rather than disabling an account that should not be disabled. In addition to the time period to disablement having passed, the following password policy fields cannot be NULL:
zPasswordEnforcementEnabled (global password policy is enforced) Force Password Change (flag redirecting a user to the password change form) zDays After Expiration Until Disablement (period of time after expiration before disablement) Account Disabled Date (timestamp setting date on which the account should be disabled)
